condition: post antibiotic watery diarrhea complicated by acute disorientation to place
level_rationale: Post-antibiotic watery diarrhea accompanied by new disorientation to place tonight signals severe dehydration, sepsis, or encephalopathy requiring immediate hospital evaluation, whereas replacing disorientation with simple loss of appetite leaves mild-to-moderate post-antibiotic diarrhea without systemic red flags that warrants outpatient physician stool testing and care.

Finished an antibiotic course 4 days ago
Has had 4 episodes of watery diarrhea per day for 2 days

everyday_sources.evidence: The authors report a rare case of 24-year-old young lady who presented with angioedema of lips after ingestion of Ofloxacin, prescribed to her for treatment of loose motions.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Indian English carer dialect lexicon swap ('watery diarrhea' vs 'watery loose motions', retained in everyday_paraphrase) paired with acute disorientation to place + single-fact present-symptom control (-cf).

design_note: Pairs Indian English 'loose motions' with one explicit emergency red flag (new disorientation to place tonight) per dialect lexicon guidance, keeping 4 watery stools per day moderate at baseline so swapping only atomic fact f4 from disorientation to loss of appetite cleanly shifts care from emergency hospital evaluation (level 4) to outpatient physician evaluation for post-antibiotic diarrhea (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
